title: The body of Christ is created flesh of the uncreated Word
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says body of Christ uncreated, and does not confess the uncreated God-Word showed incarnation from created humanity and was made man as written: anathema. How is body uncreated? Uncreated is passionless, cannot be wounded or handled. Christ rising from dead showed nails and spear-wound, body to be touched, entered shut doors, to show divinity's works and body's truth. Being God he was recognized as man; being truly man he was shown God from works.
pass_b_english: If anyone says that the body of Christ is uncreated, and does not confess that he himself — the uncreated God, the Word — showed the incarnation from created humanity and was made man, as it is written, let him be anathema.

How can a body be called uncreated? What is uncreated is also without passion: it cannot be wounded, and it cannot be handled. But Christ, rising from the dead, showed his disciples the marks of the nails and the wound the spear had made, and a body that could be touched, even while he came in when the doors were shut (John 20:19-27). He did this so that the working of the Godhead and the truth of the body might be shown together.
And while he was God, he was recognized as man in the ordinary way; and while he was truly man, he was still shown as God by his works.
source_text: Si quis dicit corpus Christi increatum, et non confitetur ipsum increatum Deum Verbum ex creata humanitate incarnationem ostendisse, factumque esse hominem sicut scriptum est, anathema sit. Quomodo enim corpus increatum dici potest? Nam quod increatum est, etiam passionis expers est, et neque vulnerari neque attrectari potest. Christus autem a mortuis resurgens clavorum et vulnerationem lancea factam corpusque suum palpandum discipulis demonstrans clausis ianuis ingressus est. Sed ut divinitatis opera et corporis veritatem ostenderet: et cum alioqui Deus esset, homo agnoscebatur; et cum esset vere homo, Deus tamen ex suis operibus ostendebatur.

choices.choice: New English from locked Latin; Crombie used only as sense check, not copied.
Too damaged to lock; Latin is copy-text; disclosed in notes.
Inline parenthetical because nails, spear, shut doors, and handling are the explication's written scene.

source_ref: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Duodecim Capita de Fide, Cap. I (anathema + interpretatio)
notes_covered: Cap. I anathema against calling Christ's body uncreated
Explication: uncreated = impassible/intangible vs risen body handled behind shut doors
Tip scope: Capita I-II only; remaining ten anathemas later
